newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian Army captures rebel chieftain in Bogota.
newsitem.headline: Colombian Army captures rebel chieftain in Bogota.

text.p: A regional chief of Colombia's oldest and largest guerrilla group was captured in Bogota on Tuesday, army sources said.

Hector Alonso Villalobos joined the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) rebel group shortly after it was set up as a pro-Soviet force in 1964, Gen. Jorge Enrique Mora, head of the army's Fifth Division, told Reuters.

Villalobos worked his way through the ranks to become head of the FARC's so-called Ninth Front, based in northwest Antioquia and central Caldas provinces, Mora said. He is wanted on charges of kidnap, extortion and rebellion.

The arrest comes two days after Damario Vargas, national leader of the Maoist-inspired people's Liberation Army (EPL), Colombia's third largest guerrilla group, was captured by the army in the northwest of the country.
The government estimates the country's three main guerrilla armies total about 12,000 men and women. Independent political analysts say the number is higher than 18,000.
